SUMMARY

Merck & Co., Inc.(MRK+4.57%)management reported that 2026 is a year of business transformation driven by new product launches and clinical de-risking of the late-phase pipeline. The company is managing a transition beyond the upcoming Keytruda loss of exclusivity by focusing on oncology advancements, cardiovascular expansion with WINREVAIR, and new immunology candidates. Management reported that while generic competition for mature products like BRIDION and Januvia will create multi-billion-dollar headwinds in 2027, recent scientific milestones in mRNA cancer vaccines and antibody-drug conjugates provide visibility into long-term growth through the 2030s. The company stated that it will continue to prioritize business development and share repurchases while investing in its expansive pipeline.

Robert Davis:Thank you, Peter. Good morning, and thank you for joining today's call. 2026 continues to be a year of substantial progress for our company, We are executing well on all fronts. Demonstrated particularly by the many new product launches now successfully underway and the important clinical milestones we are achieving that are further derisking the substantial long term opportunity of our late-phase pipeline. This momentum extends across multiple therapeutic areas and modalities and there is much more to come. With numerous significant readouts still to occur over the coming years. I am very pleased with the disciplined execution of our strategy over the past several years, is increasingly translating into meaningful clinical, regulatory, and commercial results.

The breadth of these achievements strengthens my confidence in the future of our company and our ability to deliver long term value for patients and shareholders. Turning to our third quarter results, we delivered solid performance with revenue of $18.1 billion reflecting increased contributions from new products, as well as strength in oncology and animal health. Caroline will discuss our results and the full year outlook in greater detail in a moment. We also achieved several important clinical and regulatory milestones. In oncology, last weekend's ESMO meeting showcased potential practice changing advances for several innovative programs highlighted by the first positive Phase III results from our expansive global TROFuse program for sac TMT in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.

Additional data shared at the meeting from our partner, Kelun, further support the potential of sac TMT in lung cancer and other tumor types. And we are encouraged by the landmark validation of a therapeutic cancer vaccine with positive phase 3 data presented for entismodigene as an adjuvant treatment for certain patients with melanoma. This new approach may offer a tangible opportunity to change the trajectory of a patient's cancer. In ophthalmology, we presented results from the Brunello study evaluating remygrimeg in diabetic macular edema, a significant milestone for our rapidly advancing retinal disease portfolio. And finally, in immunology, we presented encouraging Phase 2b results in HS and look forward to advancing our TL1a development program.

This year's clinical and commercial progress underlines the ongoing transformation of our business and provides us with greater visibility into the trajectory of our emerging and expansive new product portfolio. The opportunity we have to drive strong long term growth beyond the KEYTRUDA LOE period is becoming increasingly clear as we achieve these scientific and commercial milestones. As we look ahead, we will remain focused on successfully executing our launches, broadening and advancing our pipeline and making meaningful investments to realize the full potential of these opportunities. I want to recognize and thank our dedicated global teams for their ongoing commitment to delivering value for patients, shareholders, and all of our stakeholders.

And now I will turn the call over to Caroline.

Caroline Litchfield:Thank you, Robert. Good morning. As Robert noted, we delivered solid performance in the quarter driven by increasing contributions from our compelling array of important new products and continued strength in oncology and animal health. Strong commercial and operational execution continues to propel our near term performance while we invest to optimize our launches and advance our broad and deep pipeline to create long term value for patients, customers and shareholders. Now turning to our third quarter results. Total company revenues were $18.1 billion an increase of 5% or 4% excluding the impact of foreign exchange.

The following revenue comments will be on an ex exchange basis, In oncology, sales of the KEYTRUDA family of products, which includes KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX increased 6% to $8.6 billion. With global growth driven by strong uptake in earlier stage cancers, and continued robust demand for metastatic indications. Key contributors to growth included strong utilization in tumors that primarily affect women. Particularly cervical and breast cancers, as well as increased use of KEYTRUDA plus PADCEV in urothelial cancer. We also saw continued uptake in earlier stage head and neck cancer.

As expected, the timing of US customer purchases last year created a headwind to growth but this was largely offset by an increase in channel inventory which we expect to unwind in the fourth quarter. Sales of KEYTRUDA QLEX were $830 million. We continue to see adoption increase which supports our confidence in the trajectory of the product. In our broader oncology portfolio, WELIREG sales increased 58% to $370 million driven by increased use in previously treated patients and as adjuvant treatment for certain patients with renal cell carcinoma in the US, as well as continued uptake from ongoing launches in international markets. In vaccines and infectious diseases, Gardasil sales were $2 billion an increase of 14%. In The U.

S, sales grew 18% benefiting from a significant CDC purchase and price while international markets increased 6%. In pneumococcal, CAPVAXIVE sales were $263 million, an increase of 7% driven by ongoing launches in certain international markets in The U. S, sales declined 13% as increased market share was more than offset by lower adult pneumococcal vaccination rates. In RSV, WINFLONZIA sales of $187 million reflect seasonal demand and associated inventory build. In cardiometabolic and respiratory, WINREVAIR continued its momentum with global sales of $694 million an increase of 94%, reflecting strong demand from adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension as well as a benefit from channel inventory.

In the US, nearly 1.6 thousand new patients received a prescription, approximately 30 percent of whom were on therapies that did not include a prostacyclin. Outside The US, we continue to progress with ongoing launches. OHTUVAYRE sales were $184 million, reflecting continued demand from adults with COPD partially offset by a small headwind from the timing of specialty pharmacy purchases. While early, we are encouraged by the initial launch of LIPFENDRA, Prescription trends and physician feedback has been positive. Additionally, we have established programs to support access and affordability for eligible patients.

As expected, broad access will take time to build, and we remain confident in the long term opportunity for this important treatment option for adults with elevated LDL cholesterol. Our animal health business delivered growth of 3%. Companion animal sales increased 6% driven by new product launches. Livestock sales grew 2% due to higher demand for poultry products. I will now walk you through the remainder of our P&L and my comments will be on a non GAAP basis. Gross margin decreased slightly to 81.4%.

Operating expenses increased 12% to $7.4 billion reflecting increased investments to support our launches and advance our diverse early and late phase pipeline, This increase was partially offset by benefits from our ongoing multiyear optimization effort and the recognition of a portion of the external funding for TMT development. There was also a $400 million upfront charge related to the license agreement with Ceybrion compared with the $300 million business development charge a year ago. Other expense increased to $420 million primarily reflecting financing costs related to recent business development transactions. Our tax rate was 10.9%, reflecting a benefit from certain discrete items.

Taken together, earnings per share were $2.49 which includes a charge of $0.12 per share related to the Ceybrion license agreement. Now turning to our 2026 non-GAAP guidance. We have narrowed the range and raised the midpoint of both our full year revenue and EPS guidance. We now expect revenue to be between $66.8 billion and $67.3 billion representing growth of 3% to 4% including a positive impact from foreign exchange of approximately 1 percentage point using mid October rates. Our gross margin assumption remains approximately 81%, Operating expenses are expected to be between $42.4 billion and $42.9 billion Other expense is still expected to be approximately $1.4 billion We now expect a full year tax rate between 32-33%.

We assume approximately 2.48 billion shares outstanding. Taken together, we expect EPS of $2.77 to $2.82 including a positive impact from foreign exchange of approximately $0.15 using mid October rates. This range also includes the Ceybrion charge. As you consider your models, there are a few items to keep in mind. Third quarter sales benefited by approximately $550 million from favorable purchase timing in The U. S. We expect that the benefit related to KEYTRUDA and WINREVAIR to fully unwind in the fourth quarter while the majority of the benefit to vaccines primarily related to Gardasil is expected to unwind next year.

As we look forward to 2027, we recently noted an expectation for modest revenue growth For KEYTRUDA, moderating growth reflects the success we have had in reaching the eligible patients as we now approach peak revenues for certain approved indications. Additionally, we expect the German market to be impacted by policy dynamics. For BRIDION, we expect competition from multiple generics that have now entered the market. For vaccines, we are watching broader market trends given increased hesitancy and reduced utilization. Finally, we also expect underlying operating expenses to increase at a mid to high single digit rate reflecting our conviction in the significant opportunity from our expanding pipeline and the growing portfolio of new product launches.

Now turning to capital allocation, where our priorities remain unchanged. We will continue to invest in value creating opportunities that drive both near and long term growth. We remain committed to the dividend with the goal of increasing over time. Business development remains an important priority, and we retain financial flexibility within a strong investment grade credit rating to pursue additional science driven value enhancing transactions. We remain on track for approximately $3 billion in share repurchases this year.

To conclude, as we head into the fourth quarter, we remain confident in the outlook for our business Demand for our diverse portfolio of human and animal health products remained strong, and our recent launches are making increasingly meaningful contributions to growth. Our compelling innovative portfolio of pipeline assets continues to progress. Leaving us very well positioned to deliver outstanding value for patients customers, and shareholders now and into the future. With that, I would like to turn the call over to Dean.

Dean Y. Li:Thank you, Caroline. Good morning, everyone. The third quarter was marked by a number of significant clinical and regulatory. Today, I will provide updates in oncology, cardiometabolic, and respiratory, immunology, and ophthalmology. I will close by highlighting upcoming milestones. Starting with oncology, as Robert noted, the data from several pivotal studies were presented at ESMO. Which exemplify our clinical development approach and reflect how KEYTRUDA is informing our pipeline progress. ESMO marked the first presentation of detailed Phase III findings from our expansive GloboTROfuse development program for sac-TMT. Our TROF 2 directed ADC with a unique bifunctional linker. The GloboTROfuse program is guided by a 2 prong development strategy.

First, we are moving with speed and rigor to establish early leadership in multiple disease and treatment settings. Many of these first mover opportunities are in gynecologic cancers, where there remains significant unmet need. The GloboTROfuse-O5 study presented at ESMO evaluated sac TMT in patients with endometrial cancer whose disease has progressed following platinum chemotherapy and anti PD-1/L1 immunotherapy. Demonstrating a remarkable near 7-month improvement in median overall survival compared to chemotherapy alone. Endometrial cancer is 1 of the few cancers with increasing incidence and mortality rates worldwide. These patients currently face a very poor prognosis, and we look forward to continuing to work with the FDA to deliver this potential new option as quickly as possible.

Second, we are exploring the potential of sac TMT in certain types of breast and lung cancers where we believe we can be differentiated. In first line, PD L1 negative nonsquamous non small cell lung cancer results from the Optotrope lung o 6 study conducted by our partner, Kelun, showed a meaningful improvement in progression free survival sac TMT plus Keytruda over Keytruda plus chemotherapy. Raising the possibility that novel combinations may improve upon the high bar set by KEYTRUDA, plus chemotherapy. Our GloboTROfuse program includes 5 ongoing phase 3 studies in various non-small cell lung cancer settings. We plan to investigate sac TMT in combination with MK-2020 our PD 1 VEGF bispecific in first-line non-small cell lung cancer.

Engagement with the FDA has been productive and we anticipate phase III studies in this setting in the first half of 2027. Now turning to entismodigene. Our deep understanding of tumor biology continues to inform the next generation of our oncology pipeline including the development of an mRNA therapeutic cancer vaccine based on the unique mutational signature of a patient's tumor. ESMO marked the unveiling of landmark results for entismodigene, an investigational individualized neoantigen developed in collaboration with Moderna, plus KEYTRUDA as adjuvant therapy for melanoma.

Results of the Interpath o 1 study demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements in recurrence free survival and distant metastases free survival for entismodigene plus KEYTRUDA over standard-of-care KEYTRUDA in patients with completely resected stage IIb-IV melanoma. These results building on the body of evidence from the Phase 2b study, strengthen our confidence in the curative potential of entismodigene when given in combination with KEYTRUDA. We are actively engaged with the FDA on regulatory submission. Additionally, we are progressing a robust INTerpath clinical development program across a range of immune tumors including indications in earlier stages of disease, where KEYTRUDA has established efficacy. Phase 3 studies are ongoing in melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer, which are characterized by high mutational burden.

Ongoing phase 2 studies are also evaluating tumors with lower mutational burden, including certain bladder and renal cancers, to inform potential future expansion. I look forward to sharing further updates on these and other oncology programs. Now to a few regulatory updates. Subcutaneous pembrolizumab and vorhyaluronidase alfa was approved by regulatory authorities in Japan and China. In Europe, we received approval for KEYTRUDA plus PADCEV as a perioperative treatment for resectable muscle invasive bladder cancer And in The US, the FDA approved WELIREG plus LENVIMA for the treatment of patients with previously treated renal cell carcinoma. Regarding ifinatamab deruxtecan, together with Daiichi Sankyo, we made the decision to withdraw the biologic license application seeking an accelerated approval.

Multiple studies of I-DXd are ongoing in small cell lung cancer, prostate cancer, and other tumor types. Next, in cardiometabolic and respiratory, recently, the FDA approved the label update for WINREVAIR, incorporating results from the phase 3 Hyperion study providing further evidence to support its use earlier in the treatment journey for adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension. With WINREVAIR, we introduced activin signaling inhibition. A novel mechanism targeting the underlying vascular remodeling that drives disease progression. Building on the findings from the Phase 2 CADENCE trial. We are taking an important step to extend the application of activin signaling inhibition beyond group 1 PAH.

The upcoming phase 3 core study will evaluate patients with combined post and precapillary pulmonary hypertension associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. This distinct population within group 2 pulmonary hypertension has similar vascular characteristics to PH and no currently approved treatment option. Next, in immunology. Last month at EADV, positive phase 2b results were presented for tultokibart in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa making it the first anti-TL1A antibody to demonstrate positive clinical data in a dermatology indication. The study demonstrated promising clinical responses and encouraging safety profile. Based on these findings, we plan to advance tultokibart into Phase 3 development in HS.

Finally, to ophthalmology, as Robert mentioned earlier this month, results were presented from the Phase 2b/3 Brunello study the first of 2 pivotal studies evaluating remygrimeg, a novel Wnt agonist in adults with DME. Grunello achieved its primary endpoint with both doses of monthly remygrimeg demonstrating noninferior best corrected visual acuity compared to monthly zero point 5 milligram ranibizumab at 1 year. While anti VEGF therapies have transformed the treatment of DME, disease activity persists in many patients highlighting the need for new therapeutic options. Brunello provides clinical evidence that activation of the Wnt pathway can achieve noninferior efficacy to an anti VEGF agent in DME.

If confirmed in the companion Barolo trial, remygrimeg could introduce a promising new and orthogonal mechanism and help advance the field of ophthalmology toward therapeutic strategies involving multiple pathways. In closing, the breadth of these milestones reflects our progress in translating novel advances in the understanding of disease biology into potentially significant medicines across diverse therapeutic areas. Over the next 12 months, we anticipate several important clinical and regulatory milestones including in immunology for tultokibart, we are compiling data from the phase 3 ATLAS UC study and expect to share the results in the near term. In ophthalmology, the readout of the Barolo study of remygrimeg.

In cardiometabolic and respiratory, the initiation of the phase 3 core study in infectious disease, anticipated regulatory filings for islatravir plus lenacapavir the potential first once weekly oral 2 drug treatment regimen for HIV, data from the phase 3 ANCHOR study evaluating MK-1.41 thousand our investigational long acting and strain agnostic antiviral designed to prevent influenza and the data from the phase 3 expressive program of our investigational once-monthly oral HIV PrEP option alimatrovir. And finally, in oncology, the potential approval of sac-TMT in endometrial cancer and additional phase 3 readout. The anticipated regulatory filing of entismodigene and additional readouts in multiple other programs. And now I will turn the call back to Peter.

Do you feel that is now appropriately reflected in consensus estimates And then just given the R&D spend we are seeing for the company in the near term, as well as the longer term pipeline derisking we have seen, is it now fair to think about earnings growing off of this type of level as we move through the KEYTRUDA LOE, I guess, asked a different way.

Caroline Litchfield:Christopher, thank you for the question. First, if I can maybe provide everybody the headlines around our comments on 2027. And then I will answer the specific questions. For 2027, we see it as another year of investment as we invest behind our expansive pipeline and our new product launches to drive long term growth. Specifically, in 2027, we expect moderate top line growth, and that is as a result of the strong contributions we expect from our new product launches, as well as animal health, that will be partially offset by more than $2 billion of headwinds as a result of generic competition and LOE impacting BRIDION, Januvia family of products as well as Adempas.

We do expect Keytruda to continue to be an important contributor to our overall revenues although we do see growth moderating, and that is as we have reached peak penetration in a number of indications. While we also expect headwinds to price in our ex US market, and we are watching the policy dynamics in Germany. From a vaccines perspective, we have seen a benefit of a CDC buy in 2026 of approximately $250 million that will unwind in 2027. Now as we look at the rest of the P and L, gross margin will increase given the roll off of a royalty on Keytruda, As you have noted, we expect expenses to increase because we are fully investing.

Behind our strong pipeline as well as our launches. And we do expect slightly higher interest expense and a slightly higher tax rate. But all in all, 2027 marks a year of investment for strong growth in our future which is all in part to drive our strategy of how our company grows beyond the Keytruda LOE. Now as we look at that, we see the KEYTRUDA LOE as really more of a hill on the overall revenues of our company as we will in short order, then return to strong growth. As we look at consensus estimates for 2027, there are a number of different estimates from the different analysts.

And some have incorporated the messaging that we have given Many have not yet. Hopefully, this will provide clarity as to our expectations for 2027. And as we look at earnings as we move forward, we do expect to see our company have earnings as we move towards the LOE period grow. We do expect, as I have noted, a shallow dip in revenues in the initial period post the price setting through IRA and the LOE.

But to quickly return to growth and we would expect the earnings profile to probably mirror that given the expansive pipeline that we have and the continued studies that we will be doing and supporting, as well as the launches that we are coming through year over year. So headline, confident in our future, confident in our pipeline that will drive long term growth and patient benefit, and enable us to offset over time the Keytruda LOE.

Peter Dannenbaum:Great. Thank you, Christopher. Next question, please, Julie.

Dean Y. Li:Vamil, thank you very much for the question. I will just answer it in 2 parts. The first is I just wanna call out for PAH group 1, not a group 2. The field is increasingly moving to a concept of with activin signaling inhibitor, potential of remission. And you have seen that in the European guidelines that come out, and we. And what we are going to be doing in the CORAAL study, and I just wanted to be pretty clear. We are we are not expanding the patient population in any substantive way. There are details in relationship to how we are gonna execute on the trial. But we really think that, quote, unquote, this patient population that was seen in CADENCE has an incredibly high unmet need. there is no approved treatment. it is really poor prognosis, and it is also an orphan indication.

And so from CADENCE, we met primary endpoints. Reduction in PVR, and important secondary endpoints. And we are gonna initiate the Phase 3 CORAAL this year with a 0.3 milligram per kilogram dose. And with time to clinical worsening in the endpoint. And we enroll. We expect that this will be a very attractive trial for patients with group 2 pulmonary hypertension.

And that we may not be paying attention to. Thank you.

Dean Y. Li:Oh, okay. So I had a hard time hearing but I think the gist of your question relates to the TROP2 ADC that we have, our sac-TMT. And I would just highlight what was said in the in the remarks. Which is we have always had a 2-part strategy. The first part is we had recognized that when we got into the field that there were 2 TROP2s that were ahead of us. But we were actually surprised that they did not move quickly to indications outside of breast and lung, and we thought that there would be an enormous opportunity to do so.

And you see that in our clinical trials as we move very fast outside of lung and breast. There are trials that we have in lung and breast, but we have moved very fast outside of that. And this most recent Troscopy use o 5 is an evidence of that. The reason why that is important is if you look at that GloboTROfuse-O5, as a proof point, I would just call your attention to.

I think it was a presentation, I think, in 2025 or 2026 with MK 78 o 1 or Kelun-401. that is the phase 1 slash 2 endometrial cohort That was the informative information for us looking at Chinese data that allowed us to figure out how to translate that in a GloboTROfuse-O5. So the bottom line is that experience working closely with Kelun, it is not like you are gonna translate them exactly but it gives you the signal as to how you might translate it into global So that gives us confidence that the Kelun data is a really important signal for us and that we are confident that we can translate into the global trial.

And we hope to replicate that in other indications outside of lung and breast, but, clearly, as Marjorie and Eliav have talked recently, we plan to go quite aggressively in lung.

We are actively engaged with the FDA on regulatory submission. Additionally, we are progressing a robust INTerpath clinical development program across a range of immune tumors including indications in earlier stages of disease, where KEYTRUDA has established efficacy. Phase 3 studies are ongoing in melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer, which are characterized by high mutational burden.

Ongoing phase 2 studies are also evaluating tumors with lower mutational burden, including certain bladder and renal cancers, to inform potential future expansion. I look forward to sharing further updates on these and other oncology programs. Now to a few regulatory updates. Subcutaneous pembrolizumab and vorhyaluronidase alfa was approved by regulatory authorities in Japan and China. In Europe, we received approval for KEYTRUDA plus PADCEV as a perioperative treatment for resectable muscle invasive bladder cancer And in The US, the FDA approved WELIREG plus LENVIMA for the treatment of patients with previously treated renal cell carcinoma. Regarding ifinatamab deruxtecan, together with Daiichi Sankyo, we made the decision to withdraw the biologic license application seeking an accelerated approval.

Multiple studies of I-DXd are ongoing in small cell lung cancer, prostate cancer, and other tumor types. Next, in cardiometabolic and respiratory, recently, the FDA approved the label update for WINREVAIR, incorporating results from the phase 3 Hyperion study providing further evidence to support its use earlier in the treatment journey for adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension. With WINREVAIR, we introduced activin signaling inhibition. A novel mechanism targeting the underlying vascular remodeling that drives disease progression. Building on the findings from the Phase 2 CADENCE trial. We are taking an important step to extend the application of activin signaling inhibition beyond group 1 PAH.

The upcoming phase 3 core study will evaluate patients with combined post and precapillary pulmonary hypertension associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. This distinct population within group 2 pulmonary hypertension has similar vascular characteristics to PH and no currently approved treatment option. Next, in immunology. Last month at EADV, positive phase 2b results were presented for tultokibart in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa making it the first anti-TL1A antibody to demonstrate positive clinical data in a dermatology indication. The study demonstrated promising clinical responses and encouraging safety profile. Based on these findings, we plan to advance tultokibart into Phase 3 development in HS.

Finally, to ophthalmology, as Robert mentioned earlier this month, results were presented from the Phase 2b/3 Brunello study the first of 2 pivotal studies evaluating remygrimeg, a novel Wnt agonist in adults with DME. Grunello achieved its primary endpoint with both doses of monthly remygrimeg demonstrating noninferior best corrected visual acuity compared to monthly zero point 5 milligram ranibizumab at 1 year. While anti VEGF therapies have transformed the treatment of DME, disease activity persists in many patients highlighting the need for new therapeutic options. Brunello provides clinical evidence that activation of the Wnt pathway can achieve noninferior efficacy to an anti VEGF agent in DME.

If confirmed in the companion Barolo trial, remygrimeg could introduce a promising new and orthogonal mechanism and help advance the field of ophthalmology toward therapeutic strategies involving multiple pathways. In closing, the breadth of these milestones reflects our progress in translating novel advances in the understanding of disease biology into potentially significant medicines across diverse therapeutic areas. Over the next 12 months, we anticipate several important clinical and regulatory milestones including in immunology for tultokibart, we are compiling data from the phase 3 ATLAS UC study and expect to share the results in the near term. In ophthalmology, the readout of the Barolo study of remygrimeg.

In cardiometabolic and respiratory, the initiation of the phase 3 core study in infectious disease, anticipated regulatory filings for islatravir plus lenacapavir the potential first once weekly oral 2 drug treatment regimen for HIV, data from the phase 3 ANCHOR study evaluating MK-1.41 thousand our investigational long acting and strain agnostic antiviral designed to prevent influenza and the data from the phase 3 expressive program of our investigational once-monthly oral HIV PrEP option alimatrovir. The anticipated regulatory filing of entismodigene and additional readouts in multiple other programs. And now I will turn the call back to Peter.
